recommendation: Keep the audit as-is. Any future harmonization of modern medication search parameter names would be a new compatibility-impacting work-group decision, not remaining application of FHIR-3383.
issue_request: FHIR-3383 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core Pharmacy change request for DSTU1 asking to unify early MedicationAdministration `whengiven`, MedicationStatement `when-given`, and related prescription written-date search parameter naming.
initial_application: No commit explicitly tagged FHIR-3383 was found. Historical source shows the issue-era inconsistency in the old medication spreadsheets, including MedicationAdministration `whengiven`, MedicationStatement `when-given`, and MedicationPrescription `datewritten`; subsequent source evolution removed those names from the current MedicationAdministration, MedicationStatement, and MedicationRequest search parameter sources.
additional_context: MedicationAdministration, MedicationRequest, and MedicationStatement are active current build resources in source/fhir.ini. MedicationPrescription/MedicationOrder is no longer current and maps into the MedicationRequest/authoredOn lineage. Current source searches found no old medication search parameter names in the active medication administration/statement/request sources; remaining matches are a historical comment, a compatibility mapping, generated history text, or unrelated VisionPrescription/library content.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit is needed because the current authoritative search parameter bundle sources use MedicationAdministration `date`, MedicationStatement `effective`, and MedicationRequest `authoredon`, not the old inconsistent names.
